Steps.1: Review the schematic design of the hw_DAA. Check that the CAN output signals have a common mode chocke to ensure signal integrity on its signals.
Steps.2: Connect the hw_DAA to a PC. Set up the FPGA to pull data through the CAN FD signals.
Steps.3: Connect the hw_DAA to a DAA CS harness.
Steps.4: Connect the power supply to the DAA CS harness power input, using a DC power connector, banana cables, and crocodile clips (according to the attached diagram).
Steps.5: Switch on the power supply source.
Steps.6: Set 12V and 3A on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.7: Turn on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.9: Connect oscilloscope probes to CANA_P signal (before & after the common mode chocke) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.10: Set the vertical grid to 500 mV/div on both channels. Set the vertical offset to see both signals on the screen.
Steps.11: Set the horizontal grid to ~2 us/div and center the horizontal trigger position around the center of the oscilloscope screen.
Steps.12: Ensure that the attenuation is set to x10 and BW limit OFF on both channels.
Steps.13: Set the trigger level to ~2V, falling edge and source the CH1.
Steps.14: Click on the Single button to capture communication frames of the CAN FD A.
Steps.15: Check that there are not glitches in the signals after the common mode chocke.
Steps.16: Using the measure tab, measure the overshoot/undershoot and rise/fall times at each channel.
Steps.17: Take an oscilloscope screenshot (with and without zoom).
Steps.18: Repeat steps 9 to 17 with the CANA_N signal.
Steps.19: Repeat the same process with the CAN FD B signals.
